summary: Multi-chassis link aggregation joins a group of independent nodes into one logical connection. This RFC defines an EVPN port-active redundancy mode, where only one of the redundant ports is active at a time, giving a simple load-balancing and redundancy option building on RFC 7432.

eli5.summary: Two doors lead to a room, but only one is open at a time. If it gets blocked, the other opens. This is that arrangement for network links.

questions: how does evpn designated forwarder election work
subtitle: An active/standby multihoming mode for EVPN where one whole port forwards and the other waits.

tldr.problem: EVPN offers All-Active and Single-Active multihoming, but some deployments need deterministic active/standby forwarding on a whole interface, for example so that certain QoS features work correctly.
tldr.mechanism: Port-Active mode elects one Designated Forwarder per Ethernet Segment (not per VLAN) using a new Port Mode capability bit, and keeps the port on the non-DF PEs in standby. Existing EVPN election algorithms are reused at port granularity.
tldr.outcome: Operators get open-standards MC-LAG active/standby redundancy without ICCP or LDP, independent of the underlay encapsulation. All PEs in the segment must agree on the capability or the election falls back to the default procedures.

facts.label: New capability bit
facts.value: Bit 5, Port Mode Designated Forwarder Election

today: RFC 9786 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2025. It has not been obsoleted or updated, and it extends the mechanisms of RFC 7432 and RFC 8584.

sections.title: Why a Port-Active Mode
sections.content:
RFC 7432 defines two EVPN redundancy modes. All-Active gives per-flow load balancing across the multihoming PEs. Single-Active carves service so that only one PE in the redundancy relationship is active per service.

Both are widely used in data center and service provider access networks, yet some cases need active/standby multihoming at the interface level. The main reason is determinism: traffic should go through one specific interface rather than being spread statistically per flow across PEs. The RFC says this determinism is essential for certain QoS features and that the mode gives fast convergence on failure and recovery. RFC 9786 defines this Port-Active mode.
sections.eli5: Sometimes you want all the traffic to go through one particular door, not be shared between two. That makes things predictable, and the other door is ready if the first one breaks.

sections.title: MC-LAG Background
sections.content:
When a Customer Equipment (CE) device is multihomed to several PE nodes using LACP, the PEs must act as a single LACP entity so the links form one Link Aggregation Group (LAG). Historically the Inter-Chassis Communication Protocol (ICCP, RFC 7275) synchronized this state. EVPN covers the same scenario more simply, under two assumptions:

  • A CE connected to EVPN multihoming PEs MUST have a single LAG with all its links going to the PEs in the redundancy group.
  • Identical LACP parameters MUST be configured on the peering PEs, including system ID, port priority and port key.

In the RFC's topology, PE1 and PE2 serve CE1 through interfaces I1 and I2, which are members of one LAG. In Port-Active mode only one of I1 or I2 forwards and the other is standby, so all services on the active interface are active and all on the standby interface are standby. Problems from LAG misconfiguration or miswiring are out of scope.
sections.eli5: A computer plugs two cables into two different switches but pretends they are one big cable. For that to work, both switches have to be set up exactly alike.

sections.title: Port-Active Procedures
sections.content:
The RFC lists the steps for Port-Active redundancy with an EVPN LAG:

  • The Ethernet Segment Identifier (ESI) MUST be assigned per access interface, either auto-derived or manual, and the interface may be L2 or L3.
  • The Ethernet Segment (ES) MUST be configured in Port-Active mode on the peering PEs.
  • With an ESI on an L3 interface, the ES route (Route Type-4) can be the only route the PEs exchange.
  • PEs use the DF election of RFC 8584 to decide which keeps the port active, but per ES rather than per [ES, Ethernet Tag].
  • The DF MUST keep the access interface up and forwarding.
  • Non-DF routers SHOULD block all traffic in both directions, like Single-Active mode but across all VLANs. They MAY keep the interface operationally down, or, if running LACP, set the LACP state to Out of Sync (OOS) for better convergence on the move to active.
  • The primary/backup bits of the L2-Attr Extended Community SHOULD be used for faster convergence.

The RFC states that this mode is fully compliant with RFC 7432 and needs no new protocol enhancements to existing EVPN RFCs, and that it can leverage DF algorithms such as modulo and Highest Random Weight (HRW).
sections.eli5: Each pair of cables gets a name tag. The two switches pick one to be the boss for that pair. The boss keeps its door open, and the other keeps its door shut but ready.

sections.title: The Port Mode Capability Bit
sections.content:
ES routes in Port-Active mode are advertised with a new Port Mode load-balancing capability bit in the DF Election Extended Community from RFC 8584. The ES also uses the existing Single-Active procedure and signals Single-Active multihomed site redundancy mode in the Ethernet A-D per-ES route. The ESI label-based split-horizon procedures of RFC 7432 SHOULD be used to prevent transient echo packets when L2 circuits are involved.

The DF Election Capabilities field is a 2-octet bitmap. Bit 0 is the D (Don't Preempt) bit from RFC 9785, bit 1 is AC-Influenced DF from RFC 8584, and bit 3 is Time Synchronization from RFC 9722. RFC 9786 adds bit 5, Port Mode Designated Forwarder Election, which means the DF election SHOULD consider the port ES only and not the Ethernet Tags. IANA has added it to the "DF Election Capabilities" registry.
sections.eli5: Each switch holds up a small flag that says "we are doing this by whole port, not by lane." Everyone must hold up the same flag.

sections.title: DF Election at Port Granularity
sections.content:
Several election algorithms work, and the RFC says the choice does not significantly change complexity or performance compared with other redundancy modes.

  • Modulo: the default algorithm of RFC 7432, applied per ES only. Because the auto-derived ES-Import Route Target takes its value from ESI bytes 1-6, many operators differ mainly in those bytes, so bytes 3-6 are used for good entropy. With N PEs, the PE with ordinal i is DF when (Es mod N) = i, where Es is bytes 3-6 of the ESI.
  • HRW: as in RFC 8584, but the Ethernet Tag is dropped from the 32-bit CRC computation, so (V, Es) becomes (Es). The DF is the PE with the highest weight, ties go to the numerically least IP address, and the Backup DF is the next highest.
  • Preference-based: the algorithm of RFC 9785 is modified to consider the port only. Port Mode works with the Don't Preempt bit, so a recovering interface does not take back the DF role.
  • AC-Influenced: the AC-DF bit MUST be 0 when Port Mode (P=1) is advertised, and a received A=1 MUST be ignored in Port Mode election. An AC going down does not influence the election.
sections.eli5: There are a few fair ways to pick the boss, like drawing numbers or choosing the one with the biggest score. Here they all pick one boss for the whole cable pair, not one per lane.

sections.title: Convergence, Compatibility and Applicability
sections.content:
A standby port may be down, and bringing it up takes time. To speed convergence the RFC suggests prior synchronization between peers: ARP/ND caches and VRF tables for IRB and L3 services, MAC tables for L2 services. For LACP members, the "out-of-sync" or "warm-standby" state can also help.

The L2-Attr Extended Community from RFC 8214 SHOULD be advertised in the Ethernet A-D per-ES route. Only the P and B bits of the Control Flags matter here: the sender sets only P or B and all other bits and fields MUST be zero, and a receiver considers only P and B. P and B bits received on per-EVI routes SHOULD be overridden by the per-ES "parent" bits.

Older implementations that follow only RFC 7432 or RFC 8214 ignore the per-ES L2-Attr and keep their default path resolution, treating the remote ESI Label as Single-Active.

The mode fits L2 or L3 services where interface-level active/standby is required, including EVPN VPWS, L3 VPNs (RFC 4364) and EVPN IRB. The ICCP alternative of RFC 7275 needs LDP as transport, which the EVPN solution avoids, for example under VXLAN or SRv6.
sections.eli5: The spare door is shut, so opening it takes a moment. To make the swap quick, the two sides keep their notes up to date so the spare door can swing open fast.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 7432 and RFC 8584 apply. A new capability needs unanimity among the PEs. Without agreement on the new DF election procedures and Port Mode, election defaults to the RFC 8584 and RFC 7432 procedures.

The RFC points out that an attacker who changes the configuration of one PE in the ES could use this fallback to force all PEs back to the default algorithm and capabilities. The PEs could then face unfair load balancing, service disruption, traffic loss or duplicate traffic.
sections.eli5: If everyone must agree on a rule, one troublemaker who changes their answer can make the whole group drop back to the old rule and cause a mess.
